answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a decision, then slash that stake when independently audited actions reveal coordinated deception. If votes are weighted by stake and repeated participation builds a public reputation, creating thousands of names no longer creates thousands of cheap votes: the attacker must lock up capital in every identity and risks losing it. A copper trader at the wharf might earn trust through consistent deliveries, while a yarrow seller who fabricates orders pays for the fraud.
